question: How do short rolling and terminal MOSS windows cooperate to make live mode immediate convergent and file-quality after stop?

citations.quote: The audio interval sent to one fresh MOSS decode. Longer windows give more context but become eligible later.
One owner per interval; ordered non-overlapping segments; forward-only frontier; immutable base commits; stale work changes nothing; rolling PCM bounded to 2 × W seconds.
Rolling failure leaves the visible surface unchanged. Stale work is refused. Terminal failure keeps capture successful and preserves the best rolling surface with a failed finalization status.

answers.note: Five primitives, monotonic ownership rules, authority transitions, and explicit failure behavior form a coherent rebuildable model.

citations.quote: WebRTC VAD reports speech on ordered, gap-free observations. The endpoint accumulates audio. Enough silence closes naturally. Continuous speech crossing the hard boundary emits hard_cap, resets speech state, and starts the next exact partition.
The witness sends a longer retained-audio window through the same MOSS model, then grants it authority over one central interval.
Context is input; ownership is publication authority. Separating them is the central algorithm.

answers.note: The report explains the endpoint, rolling witness, coordinate mapping, reconciliation, and authority transfer at causal algorithm depth.

citations.quote: The suffix may display provisionally; immutable history records it.
A proposal begins at the frontier and fits committed audio.
Finalization fails visibly; rolling remains.

answers.note: All three authority states receive distinct acceptance, replacement, refusal, and fallback behaviors, supplemented by the five phase outcomes.

citations.quote: A short MOSS request gives immediate provisional words; a longer overlapping MOSS witness replaces them with a monotonic rolling transcript; a stop-time file-style pass produces the final surface.
Correct words do not guarantee correct speakers. MOSS local S01 is meaningful only inside one request.
At 60 minutes, each terminal request still hears at most 150 seconds. Window count grows linearly; per-request prefill does not.

answers.note: The claims depend on MOSS joint decoding, WeSpeaker identity reconciliation, measured seam behavior, and the specific 150/120 terminal policy.

citations.quote: Pressure: continuous speech can delay publication and grow requests. Choice: cap at 2.5 seconds. Alternative: wait only for silence. Trade-off: bounded latency/memory versus arbitrary speech seams.
Measured 10 / 5 rolling reached WER .1289, recovering 74% of the gap to file. Five seconds at every seam worsened WER to .2298.
If 10% of regions need four extra views, regional extra work is roughly 0.10 × 4 = 0.40 of one blanket pass, not four whole-meeting passes.

answers.note: Material choices consistently expose pressure, alternatives, measured trade-offs, and operational consequences.

citations.quote: A 1-second base can improve L1 only if E3 proves timely L2 correction and witness-owned speaker evidence. Until then, keep 2.5 seconds.
MOSS/vLLM exposes no reusable encoder or decoder state across requests. Each overlap re-encodes and re-decodes.
If they agree, publish without another view. If they disagree, add phase-shifted views only there and cache exact-interval embeddings.

answers.note: A reader can evaluate preview duration, rolling schedules, compute reuse, and targeted extra views using explicit predictions and promotion gates.

citations.quote: A hard cap lands inside between. The exact phrase is illustrative; the error concentration and correction measurements are recorded evidence.
Steady-state example. A rolling request hears ten seconds but owns its five-second middle. Start/end edge rules give leftovers to the nearest valid owner.
Adjacent windows 0–150 and 120–270 overlap for 30 seconds. Their midpoint, 135, transfers ownership. Every time point has one final owner and every interior seam has context.

answers.note: The honestly simulated sentence and ownership diagrams expose seam damage, correction, terminal replacement, and exact boundary rules.

citations.quote: The mission is not “make every first guess perfect.” The user accepts temporary mistakes. The mission is: publish quickly, improve predictably, then settle once.
Current live requests carry no meeting history. The seam failure repeats; it does not accumulate. Bounded witnesses preserve that property.
The exact interval whose words and speaker evidence one result may publish.
